sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by anti-Flag immunofluorescence microscopy in A549 LRP8-KO cells overexpressing Flag-tagged LRP8 (L3); surface expression also confirmed by supplementary flow/imaging in K562 cells for Flag-ApoER2 iso1 (L1/L2). Receptor function not measured in these clips.
sites.rationale: LRP8 (ApoER2) is a type I single-pass transmembrane receptor: the ectodomain spans residues 33–825, the TM helix 826–848, and the cytoplasmic tail 849–963. The only extracellular terminus is the mature N-terminus beginning at residue 33 (after cleavage of the 1–32 signal peptide). A surface-detected Flag tag on a full-length membrane-anchored construct can only reside at this terminus; the junction is therefore insert_after_residue = 32 (between the last SP residue A32 and the first mature residue A33), computed from the landmarks. Python confirmed seq[31]='A' and seq[32]='A'. The tag position is 793 residues from the TM boundary, satisfying the ≥3-residue constraint with large margin. Flag-tagged full-length LRP8 overexpressed in A549 LRP8-KO cells and immunostained with anti-Flag antibody by fluorescence microscopy, confirming surface display of the tagged construct (L3). Independently corroborated by Flag-tagged full-length ApoER2 isoform 1 (residues 1–963, same protein) with surface expression confirmed in K562 cells (L1/L2, same paper). No ledger line names the insertion residue; LRP8 is a type I single-pass receptor with a 793-residue N-terminal ectodomain (residues 33–825) and an intracellular C-terminus (849–963), leaving exactly one extracellular terminus.

sources.claim: Scale bar, 20 μm. c (left panel) , WT and A549 LRP8 -KO cell lines as well as A549 LRP8 -KO cells overexpressing Flag-tagged LRP8 were immunostained with an anti-Flag mAb and visualized by fluorescence microscopy.

literature_notes: L1/L2 (PMC12827466) independently corroborate the N-terminal Flag tag on full-length ApoER2 isoform 1 (residues 1–963) with surface confirmation in K562 cells; they are the same paper as L3's corroboration and pin the same junction, so no additional site is added. L4/L5 (pcDNA3-HA-ApoER2, pEGFP-HA-ApoER2, citing Cuitino et al. 2005) and L6 (FM4-GFP HA-ApoER2 with heterologous hGH signal sequence) also describe HA-tagged full-length ApoER2 constructs but neither clip states the insertion residue nor confirms surface expression; they corroborate the same N-terminal position but do not add a new site or raise the validation level. The domain-swap constructs in L1 (LA1-Flag residues 46–85 + 334–963, LA2-Flag, etc.) are membrane-anchored but chimeric/truncated; the Flag position within each is not stated, so no internal site can be pinned from them. No ledger line reports an internal loop insertion or a C-terminal surface tag for LRP8/ApoER2.
